intervals.label: GALLEX + GNO operation
intervals.note: Span from the GNO collaboration's final paper (gallium observations at LNGS lasted from May 14, 1991 through April 9, 2003); stored at year/month precision.
intervals.quote: gallium based solar observations at LNGS (first in GALLEX, later in GNO) lasted from May 14, 1991 through April 9, 2003

intervals.label: shut down
intervals.note: Terminal event from the GNO collaboration's final paper (GNO terminated after solar runs performed between May 20, 1998 and April 9, 2003); stored at month precision.
intervals.quote: The GNO experiment is now terminated after altogether 58 solar exposure runs that were performed between May 20, 1998 and April 9, 2003.

placements.note: Placed at site:lngs-hall-a. The cited GNO final paper names LNGS and the 1991-2003 span but does not name Hall A specifically.
placements.quote: gallium based solar observations at LNGS (first in GALLEX, later in GNO) lasted from May 14, 1991 through April 9, 2003

target_mass.locator: GNO Collaboration final paper (Phys. Lett. B 616, 174; arXiv:hep-ex/0504037), Sec. 1 (Introduction)
target_mass.note: The GNO final paper gives the gallium chloride target as 100 tons containing 30.3 tons of gallium; the MPIK Heidelberg GALLEX/GNO history page gives the same 30.3 t of gallium in a GaCl3-HCl solution of total weight 101 t.
target_mass.quote: in a 100-ton gallium chloride target (containing 30.3 tons of gallium)

summary.plain: A huge tank of gallium-laced liquid buried in an Italian mountain; when a low-energy solar neutrino hits a gallium atom, it turns into a germanium atom that scientists then count.
summary.technical: Radiochemical gallium detector, 30.3 t Ga as 101 t GaCl3-HCl solution, at LNGS Hall A; 71Ga(νe,e⁻)71Ge reaction, chemically extracted and counted in campaigns rather than observed in real time.

technology.locator: MPIK Heidelberg GALLEX/GNO history page, sections "GALLEX: a radiochemical GALLium EXperiment to detect solar pp neutrinos" and "The GALLEX detector and 71Ge extraction procedure"
technology.note: The reaction, the GaCl3-HCl target, the chemical extraction of germanium and its counting in proportional counters are described by MPIK Heidelberg, the lead institute of GALLEX; the GNO final paper gives the same reaction in a 100-ton gallium chloride target. The technology classes have no radiochemical value, so the class is 'other' and the radiochemical gallium technique is described in this free-text field instead.
technology.quote: Gallium as target allows neutrino interaction via νe + 71Ga → 71Ge + e–. ... Germanium is removed from the solution as volatile germanium chloride (GeCl4). ... Finally, it is placed together with Xenon into a miniaturized proportional counter.
technology.value: Radiochemical gallium detector: solar neutrinos capture on 71Ga to produce 71Ge, which is chemically extracted and counted; the target is a gallium trichloride-hydrochloric acid solution, not an electronic real-time detector
